title: 2 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 11
description: Ten questions on 2 Corinthians 11: godly jealousy, false apostles who masquerade, and a long list of hardships ending with an escape from Damascus.

questions.text: What kind of jealousy does the writer say he has over the readers?
questions.explanation: He says he is jealous over them with a godly jealousy, having married them to one husband to present them as a pure virgin to Christ.

questions.text: Whom does the writer say the serpent deceived in his craftiness?
questions.explanation: He fears that their minds might be corrupted, just as the serpent deceived Eve in his craftiness.

questions.text: On what terms did the writer preach God's Good News to them?
questions.explanation: He asks whether he sinned in humbling himself so they might be exalted, because he preached God's Good News to them free of charge.

answers.text: For a share of the profit

questions.text: Who supplied the measure of his need while he was with them?
questions.explanation: He says he was not a burden on anyone, because the brothers supplied the measure of his need when they came from Macedonia.

answers.text: The brothers who came from Macedonia

questions.text: As what does the writer say Satan masquerades?
questions.explanation: He says it is no wonder that false workers masquerade, for even Satan masquerades as an angel of light.

answers.text: As a shepherd of the flock
As a teacher of the law

questions.text: How many times did he receive forty stripes minus one from the Jews?
questions.explanation: He says that five times he received forty stripes minus one from the Jews.

questions.text: How long had he been in the deep, according to his own account?
questions.explanation: After telling of beatings, a stoning and shipwrecks, he says he has been a night and a day in the deep.

questions.text: Besides outward hardships, what does he say presses on him daily?
questions.explanation: He says that besides the things that are outside, what presses on him daily is anxiety for all the assemblies.

answers.text: Hunger and thirst on his journeys

questions.text: If he must boast, what does he say he will boast of?
questions.explanation: He says that if he must boast, he will boast of the things that concern his weakness.

answers.text: The things that concern his weakness

questions.text: How did he escape the governor in Damascus?
questions.explanation: He says he was let down in a basket through a window by the wall, and so escaped the hands of the governor who wanted to arrest him.

answers.text: He was hidden by a friend in the market
He was released by the governor himself
He walked out openly through the gate
He was let down in a basket through a window
